findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: There was no sanitizer observed in the deli kitchen as food was being portioned during today’s inspection. Discussed with PIC. A sani bucket was made. Ensure that there is a sanitizer present and at the appropriate concentration at all times.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(E) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (E) If a chemical SANITIZER other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed mops being dried in mop bucket basin. Discussed proper mop drying procedures with PIC. Ensure that mops are hung to dry, either over the wringer basket or on the wall. CORRECTED PIC placed the mops so that the mop heads were hanging over the wringer basket.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: There was a glue insect trap placed directly over the triple, exposing clean dishes to possible contamination. There were at least five dead flies present on the trap. Discussed the need to place the trap in a different location to prevent insect fragments from falling onto clean dishes. Ensure that insects traps are placed in a manner that prevents contamination of food, food contact surfaces, dishes, and utensils.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: There wasn't a sanitizer solution available while food preparation was occurring. Discussed with PIC and a solution was created and tested at 400ppm (quat). Be sure that a sanitizer solution is available if food preparation is occurring to ensure that food contact surfaces are getting properly sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Several areas in the kitchen were observed accumulated with grease and/or food debris:
- floors and drains underneath the rotisserie ovens
- floors around both chicken fryers
- Sides of fryers

Ensure that cleaning occurs in these areas as frequent as necessary to prevent build up of grease and food debris.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: At the start of the inspection, the wasn't a Certified Food Protection Manager available. Food preparation was occurring during the inspection. Shortly afterwards, a CFPM arrived to correct the violation. Ensure that there is always a CFPM available whenever food preparation is occurring.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Several sanitizer bottles throughout the facility were testing at 0ppm (q). The PIC mentioned that the sani bottles were prepared using the dispenser in the bakery’s dish room. The chemical directly dispensing from the dispenser was also testing at 0ppm (q). The facility was instructed to use sanitizer from the chemical dispenser in the other dish room (deli). PIC refilled each sani bottle and the chemical tested at 200ppm (q) to correct the violation.
findings.citation_text: 4-703.11(C)(4) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations, including the application of SANITIZING chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA registered label use instructions by providing: (4) A contact time used in relationship with a combination of temperature, concentration, and PH that, when evaluated for efficacy, yields SANITIZATION as defined in 1-201.10(B).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

The bottom of the yogurt cooler was observed to have an accumulation of trash on the lining. The facility uses a paper lining at the bottom of the coolers. The facility is getting new coolers soon and it was recommended to make sure that the bottom of those coolers stay clean and that the lining is changed more often. Nonfood contact surfaces should be maintained cleaned.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed food in the end cap of  A/7 to be holding food between 45F and 52F. These items were deli trays with cheese and meat that read keep refrigerated on the label. The deli trays are in a unit with an independent thermometer which reads 41F. The trays were taken to deli to be marked down and discarded. A ticket was placed for the unit to be evaluated. 

Also, take and bake individually wrapped pizzas are observed to be between 48F and 50F in the other end cap area of the A/7 bank. The pizzas were below an area where pizzas were stocked to the point that they cut off air flow to the items on the bottom shelf of the cooler. The items were pulled and set at deli to be thrown away. 
Take great care when stocking foods that require temperature control for safety. The violation is considered corrected on site.

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Inspector observed white containers of food service utensils to be soiled in the bottom with crumbs and dust. Remove utensils, properly wash and sanitize the utensils and containers. Correct and maintain the correction for the next routine inspection. 

4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the hot food case and the bottom of the stainless two door cooler near the coffee pot is soiled in the bottom. Clean and maintain these items free of accumulated food soil. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed keys and a phone on the prep surface next to the 3 door cooler. These items were removed. Develop a good habit for personal items and store all personal items properly. 

6-305.11: (A) Dressing rooms or dressing areas shall be designated if EMPLOYEES routinely change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

Observed an employee go to the back to get more deli meat and return with the same gloves on. She removed gloves and put new on but did not wash hands between the glove changes. Also, observed an employee drop a gove on top of his shoe, bend over to pick it up and began to put the glove on his hand. The employee was stopped immediately and coached on hand washing and proper glove use. The other employee was also coached on glove use and hand washing. 
Develop proper hand washing techniques and training for employees handling ready to eat food.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

Observed employee make a phone call, to call for a manager, then proceed to put on food service gloves in order to wait on a customer. The employee was stopped and coached on when to wash hands along with proper hand washing technique.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the spray nozzle at the 3 compartment sink to have large amount of build-up and debris on and under the nozzle, as well as the squeezer. Ensure non food-contact surfaces are washed, rinsed, sanitized as needed to prevent debris. Discussed with PIC. Ensure employees are aware.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11(C)(2) (Pf) PIC does not demonstrate the responsibility of preventing the transmission of foodborne disease by employees that may cause food borne disease. Discussed related section of the food code.  Reference 2-102.11(C)(2).

Observed facility lacking appropriate paperwork regarding: employee health reporting agreements, requirements for symptomatic employees for reporting (exclusion and restriction), and requirements for diagnosed food service employees. Discussed paperwork with PIC. PIC indicated that CFM/deli manager likely had this paperwork. Discussed completing employee health reporting agreements with all food handlers in deli area. 1st Re-Inspection will occur 1/13/2020.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12  (P) Food employee improperly washed hands. Food employees shall properly wash their hands and exposed portion of their arms for at least 20 seconds, with approved soap and drying methods, according to this section of the food code. Reference 2-301.12.

Observed employee improperly washing hands: touched paper towel dispenser to obtain paper towels after properly washing hands. In order to hinder cross-contamination, ensure paper towels are ready before washing hands. COS.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14  (P) Employee changed gloves without washing hands between tasks. Food employee must practice good hygiene by properly washing hands when changing tasks. Reference 2-301.14.

Observed employee helping inspector with questions regarding sanitization at the 3 compartment sink and sani buckets, then proceed to help customer with deli meat without washing hands between tasks. Employee only changed gloves. Discussed importance of washing hands between tasks and changing gloves. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114  (P) Quaternary ammonium sanitizer measured 100 ppm at three compartment sink. Maintain concentration at 200 ppm to 400 ppm as indicated on manufacturer's label.  Reference 4-501.114.

Observed improper quaternary ammonium sanitizer concentration at 3 compartment sink, 100 ppm. Discussed with PIC the need for quat to remain between 200 to 400 ppm. Inspector suggested leaving facility test strips near the 3 compartment sink area in order to regularly test levels. COS.

Observed lack of sanitization bucket upon start of inspection. Facility did not have a sanitization bucket made. Discussed need for sanitization bucket during hours of operation. COS.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text:
6-202.11  (C) Lighting was found not shielded or otherwise protected in the reach-in freezer area. Light bulbs shall be shielded, coated, or otherwise shatter-resistant in areas where there is exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, linens; or unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Reference 6-202.11.

Observed one of the reach-in freezers to have the light bulb hanging from socket. Discussed repairs with PIC.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: PA 100-0367 (C) All CFPMs at a high risk facility should have completed an ANSI accredited allergen awareness program. Handout was given to the PIC and they were instructed to ensure that all CFPMs complete an accredited course prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
In hot holding display unit: general tso's chicken 116F-125F, chicken wings 130F. Both items located on furthest left side of the unit. Other food items measured above 135F. Noted a few heat bulbs which were burnt out above the food items. Food items were discarded. Please monitor hot holding food items to ensure above 135F. 

->Hot held foods must be maintained with temperatures greater than 135F. Please monitor and verify proper food temperatures. Reference 3-501.16(A)(1).

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Door handle on the sliding door where ham chubs are kept was found missing and in disrepair. PIC indicated item is to be repaired soon. 
Sealant on 3 compartment sink joining equipment to the wall found missing in areas. Please re-seal as needed. 

->Equipment components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted in accordance with manufacturer's specifications. Reference 4-501.11.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.citation_text:
2-401.11. Employee was observed chewing gum in the ware washing area while demonstrating the proper procedure for cleaning and sanitizing the food thermometer used for checking fried chicken cook temperatures. Employee stated she was getting ready to leave for the day just prior to the manager asking her to clean and sanitize the food thermometer. The employee was in the deli area behind the counter when asked to clean the thermometer and already had gum in her mouth. Employee left for the day. Management was advised to speak with staff about eating only in designated areas, including gum/candy, and to not place gum/candy in their mouths until they are out of the food prep/service areas.

Employees shall eat, drink, or use any form of tobacco only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single service and single use articles; or other items needing protection can not result.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11(C) While speaking with deli manager about cleaning frequency for slicers it was discovered the slicers are not getting washed, rinse, and sanitized up to every 4hrs after continuous use. Manager noted that up to every 4hrs slicers are soaked with sanitizer and wiped down. Detail cleaning and sanitizing that involves disassembly of the slicer for components to be cleaned and sanitized at the 3 part sink and the blade and base to be cleaned and sanitized in place occurs at the end of operations daily. Deli manager stated the frequency/process for deli slicers can be changed if necessary. Management was advised to have the deli staff change the procedure and make sure all slicer components used for deli meats and cheeses are properly cleaned and sanitized up to every 4hrs after continuous use. 

Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils used with time/temperature control for safety food shall be cleaned and sanitized throughout the day at least every 4 hours. (see general comments for additional information)

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 The following nonfood contact surfaces were observed to be soiled:
A) bottom inside upright coolers and freezer (crumbs/food splash);  and
B) Electrolux oven - general surfaces and drain line (dust/debris/buildup).
Clean the abovementioned items

Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15 Puddling water was observed at the corner by the handsink closest to the hot holding case. A leak was observed at the connection behind the foot peddles of the handsink. Deli manger noted that management was aware, and a work order has been placed for the deli handsink and a bakery handsink with a similary issue.

A Plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair. Repair the handsink according to Illinois and local plumbing code.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the door at one of the deli coolers not properly functioning (duct tape). Repair the door.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
1) Observed the door at one of the deli coolers not properly functioning (Duct tape). Repair the door. 2) Observed wet cardboard underneath the cheese that a condenser is not working properly. Repair the cooler.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Observed no paper towels at the handwashing sink in the kitchen. Paper towels were replaced during the inspection.
750-1120e A supply of soap and and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: Observed no thermometers in the coolers holding deli meats. Provide thermometers.
findings.citation_text: 750.150(a) All hot units that contain potentially hazardous foods shall contain  a conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
Observed an employee with gloved hands pull her sleeves up and touch ready to eat foods. The employee was notified and make sure to switch gloves and wash hands in between uses.
750-530e Employees shall maintain a high degree of personal cleanliness and shall conform to good hygienic practices during all working periods in the food service establishment.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the microwave to be soiled near the fryer area. Clean the non-food contact surfaces.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Observed no paper towels at a handwashing sink. Replace paper towels.
750-1120e A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed no floor drain cover in the mop sink. Replace the floor drain.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
Observed the mop stored incorrectly. Invert the mop or hang to dry.
750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: Observed missing thermometers in some prep coolers. Provide thermometers in all cold holding units.
findings.citation_text: 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:

750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed degreaser stored above single service soup cups. The degreaser was removed to correct the violation.
750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: (1) Observed two containers of shredded rotisserie chicken date marked 10/30 and 11/11. Chicken labeled 10/30 had an internal temperature of 50 F and the chicken labeled 11/11 had an internal temperature of 57 F. Management and deli employees were unsure of when the chicken had been prepared. Chicken was discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that products are properly date marked to ensure they are used within the 7 day period. (2) Observed cheese in the refrigerated display unit stocked above the air curtain for the unit. Cheese temperatures were recorded at 54 F and 48 F. Cheese was voluntarily discarded to correct the violation (four units of panner cheese at 8 oz each and two units of blue cheese at 6 oz each). Ensure that refrigerated units are stocked in a manner that maintains food at 41 F or below.750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: (1) the exterior of the two door cooler with food splash, (2) the bottoms of the six prep table/slicer table coolers with food debris, (3) the seals on the prep table/slicer table coolers with food debris, (4) the ends and exteriors of the slicer table/prep table coolers with food debris, (5) the three shelf carts with food debris, (6) the exterior of the lid caddy with food splash, (7) the tracks of the hot holding case with food debris, (8) the exterior of the hot holding case with food splash, (9) the exterior of the hot holding case by the blast chiller with food debris, (10) the interior of the hot holding cabinet with food debris. Clean and maintain all non-food contact surfaces. 750-300e All non-food contact surfaces shall be properly cleaned.

findings.title: Water source safe, hot, and cooled under pressure
findings.comment:
Observed no hot water at the hand washing station behind the sushi prep station at the beginning of the inspection. Management turned on hot water from underneath the hand washing sink. Hand washing sinks shall always have hot water accessible to promote proper hand washing practices. 
750-1120 Each lavatory shall be provided with hot and cold water tempered by means of a mixing valve or combination faucet.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: (1) Observed the drain under the three compartment sink to be soiled with a heavy accumulation of food debris and random articles. Clean and maintain drain to provide proper drainage and prevent pest harborage. (2) Observed the floor behind the convection oven to be soiled with an accumulation of food debris and dust. (3) Observed the floor under the shelving units in the dish area to be soiled with an accumulation of food debris, random articles, and dust. (4) Observed the floor under the rotisserie area to be soiled with an accumulation of food debris, grease, and dust.  Clean and maintain floors. 750-1220 Floors shall be kept free of accumulated soil, dirt, and food debris.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: (1) Observed the walls in the dish room to be soiled with a heavy accumulation of food splash. (2) Observed the walls in the rotisserie area to be soiled with an accumulation of food splash. 750-1210a Walls and ceiling shall be kept free of accumulated soil, build-up.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment:
The hot holding unit with bbq,  macaroni and cheese, and mashed potato is not maintaining the food at 135 or above.  Upon arrival, the foods are 105F, 117F and 98F respectively. 
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage, display and service.(41°F or below, or 135°F or above). These foods were discarded in the garbage. The hot holding unit was checked again upon conclusion of the inspection and the unit is holding macaroni and cheese at 130F and Mashed potato at 117F. The foods will be given a four hour time as a control limit so that they can be sold and the unit used. A time log will be maintained. A follow up inspection will be conducted after the unit has been repaired or replaced.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

findings.comment: Thermometer absent from hot holding area under deli hot case. 750.150(a) All hot units that contain potentially hazardous foods shall contain  a conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F Provide thermometer.
